findings.message: the pattern matches 12 of 13 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is "15-Oct-2026 14:56:43.951 client @0x760106c14c90 172.21.0.3#41131 (corp.example): zone transfer 'corp.example/AXFR/IN' denied". Of the 5 patterns, the closest to it is '^%{DATA:timestamp} client @%{NOTSPACE:client_object} %{IP:client_ip}#%{INT:client_port} \\(%{DATA:query_name}\\): query: %'. the pattern matches up to %{WORD:query_class}, which fails on "corp.example): zone transfer 'corp.examp". The capture before it, %{DATA:query_name}, matched only '' and stopped at 'corp.example' - it is too narrow, and that is the one to widen. %{WORD} matches letters, digits and underscore only - NOT a dot, hyphen, colon or slash. For a hostname use %{HOSTNAME}, for any run of non-space characters use %{NOTSPACE} If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.
